title: A Major Shift in How Girls View Marriage
author: Institute for Family Studies
source: Institute for Family Studies Digest, January 26, 2026
summary: For the first time in modern polling, girls expect marriage less than boys do. This historic reversal reflects changing cultural narratives around women's independence, career priorities, and skepticism about marriage. While this trend might appear progressive, it raises important questions about the foundations of family formation and whether young women understand the personal and social benefits of marriage. IFS research shows that married women report higher happiness and life satisfaction than their unmarried counterparts, yet cultural messaging emphasizes female independence from marriage rather than the genuine goods marriage provides.
points: Girls now expect marriage less than boys—a historic reversal with major implications for family formation.
Young women have absorbed cultural messaging that marriage is a constraint on female achievement and freedom.
Research shows married women report higher happiness, yet this data is rarely discussed in mainstream culture.
The shift in girls' expectations about marriage reflects broader cultural skepticism about family institutions.
quotes: For the first time, girls expect marriage less than boys do—a major shift in how a new generation views family.
